messages.content: I'm trying to set up pricing for my SaaS product that offers a one-time form filing service and an annual subscription for unlimited updates and filings. Given that my competitor charges $99 for a one-time filing and $149 for an annual subscription, while another competitor charges $149 and $249 respectively, help me determine a competitive price for a customer located at 34.0522, -118.2437? Let's use a base price of $100 and ensure we don't go below $90.

function.name: calculate_dynamic_pricing
function.description: Calculates the price for a service based on the geolocation of the customer, ensuring a minimum price threshold is met. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

geolocation.description: The geolocation of the customer in the format of 'Latitude, Longitude', such as '36.2522, -105.3437'.

base_price.description: The base price for the service before location-based adjustments. This is a float type value.

minimum_price.description: The minimum price to charge regardless of the customer's location. This is a float type value.

location_multiplier.description: Multiplier applied to the base price based on customer's geolocation. A higher multiplier indicates a more expensive area. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: We need to use the function calculate_dynamic_pricing. Provide geolocation, base_price=100, minimum_price=90. We can optionally provide location_multiplier. We need to determine a competitive price for a customer located at 34.0522, -118.2437. The competitor prices: $99 and $149, $149 and $249. So we want to set a price that is competitive. We might want to set a price slightly lower than competitor's lowest one-time filing ($99) but above minimum ($90). So maybe $95. But we need to use the function to calculate dynamic pricing. The function will apply location multiplier. We can set location_multiplier maybe 1.0 or something. But we can also compute a multiplier based on location. But we don't have data. We can just set multiplier 1.0. Then the function will return price. But we need to produce a price. The function returns any. We need to call it. Let's call with geolocation "34.0522, -118.2437", base_price 100, minimum_price 90, location_multiplier 1.0. That will return 100. But we want to adjust to competitive price. We can set location_multiplier less than 1 to reduce price. For example 0.95 gives 95. That is above minimum. So we can set location_multiplier 0.95. Then price = 95. That is competitive. So we call function with location_multiplier 0.95. Then we output the result.
